posts.author: Holomark
posts.content_md:
Ed, 

That picture of you hurts my eyes. Is it my monitor or is there some reason for the blurry/out of focus image?

Mark

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Sorry if that image offends, but a nice sharp one might be harsher on your eyes!

You’re not the first one to comment on this image, I got an e-mail from Dr. Laser, Jason Sapon:

“Holy crap! Is that what you look like now???? I must look like death by comparison!” So I guess I must look like holy crap! We’ll have to sort this out!

Curiously enough, I don't know who took this picture of me! At a certain point in the semester during the Physics of Light class in the Harrington College of Design’s Digital Photography Department I bring in my film cameras for students to look at and through. Sometimes they are even bold enough to take a picture! So this was on a roll of film from that experience, and I have no clue as to who took it! I think it's appropriate as it looks like I am looking through a lens.

I wanted to run a different image, of me doing the aberration demo, note the pincushion distortion on the door. But the photographer didn’t reply with permission to reproduce in a timely manner, so we didn’t want to step on anyone’s toes at the CPC. But here it is here!

[](https://holographyforum.org/forum/download/file.php?id=2531&mode=view)

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
I guess my self-effacing humor doesn't transmit well over the web. Need to see live and in person.

I like this image because it makes you really think about what you are looking at. Plus it takes decades off my face, cheaper than plastic surgery.

No video tapes were made, however the "classroom handouts" for the event are up at my new web site, (a transplant of my grad school site, slowly being revitalized), at [http://edweslystudio.com/Photo/CPCLecture/index.html](http://edweslystudio.com/Photo/CPCLecture/index.html)
